# Best 65W GaN charger for a laptop and a phone

**My pick: Anker 735 (Nano II 65W), $29.99.** It's a well-reviewed 3-port charger that powers a laptop and a phone at once.
[Buy at Newegg](https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3)

- **Single device:** a full 65W from either USB-C port.
- **Laptop + phone:** 45W + 20W on the two USB-C ports, which is fine for a MacBook Air-class laptop plus a fast-charging phone.
- **All three ports in use:** it drops to 40W / 12W / 12W.
- **Size and warranty:** about the size of an AirPods Pro case, with an 18-month warranty.
- **Cable:** none is included.
- **PPS:** Anker's spec sheet lists it ([Anker](https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY)). One review site says otherwise ([Laptopbee](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-65w-usb-c-chargers/)), so check if you need it for a Samsung phone.

## Other good options

- **Baseus Enercore 67W (CJ11), about $29.99.** It was Tom's Hardware's best midrange charger. It held full wattage through testing and ran the coolest of the group. It has a built-in retractable USB-C cable plus two more USB-C ports, so it suits travel. [Tom's Hardware review, with buy links](https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/usb/best-usb-chargers)
- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W.** It was the top pick in one review for travel. It weighs 113g, has three ports, and ships with US, UK and EU plug heads. With two devices it splits 45W + 20W, and the USB-A port tops out at 22.5W. [Smart Gadget Kit review](https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/)
- **Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W, 2-pack for $49.99.** This is a good fit if you want one charger for home and one for your bag, or if you have a Samsung Galaxy, since it supports PPS. The laptop port drops to 45W when you charge a second device. [Dealectric listing (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u)

## Things to know

- On every 65W charger, the full 65W is only available when a single device is plugged in. With a phone connected, the laptop gets about 45W. That's fine for most thin-and-light laptops but slower for a 65W gaming or workstation laptop.
- If you have a 14" or 16" MacBook Pro or another high-draw laptop, consider a 100W charger instead.
- The Review sites vary in rigor. Tom's Hardware did instrumented testing, while the others are mostly roundups, so I leaned on manufacturer specs for port splits.

If you tell me your laptop model and phone, I can narrow it down further.
